tagline.text: Waves of green hills and grazing cattle above the sea north of Basco

location.label: Location
location.text: Along the national road in Barangay San Antonio, Basco, Batanes

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100–1,000 (per person; Basco tricycle transport, excluding flights and lodging)

children.text: Vayang Rolling Hills are green grassy hills about 2.5 km north of central Basco. Soft ridges where cows, goats and carabaos graze run all the way to the sea, and the hills are known as a sunrise and sunset photo spot.
Vayang Rolling Hills lie along the national road in Barangay San Antonio, north of central Basco. Depending on the travel site it is also called Vayang Ranch, and it is described as about
2.5 km
from Basco town. On the map it is about
2.7 km
north of Naidi Hills, where Basco Lighthouse stands, around
10 minutes
by tricycle. One travel guide says it takes
10–15 minutes
by tricycle or van from Basco Airport.

In a phrase, the scenery here is grassland pouring down to the sea. One trip report describes the slopes as rising and diving gently into a crumpled terrain, with the grass-covered hills serving as a feeding and resting ground for cows, goats and carabaos. With no tall mountains or buildings the sky opens wide, and on a clear day blue sky, green hills and blue sea layer one behind another. Winds blow hard enough to lay the grass flat in one direction, and that is a hallmark of photos taken here.

For travelers, this hill is a place where you do not need to do anything. Sources say there is not much to do besides taking photos and enjoying the view, and describe about an hour as enough. Picnics, light walks and stargazing are said to be possible, but it is dark and windy at night, so plan around daytime. Sunrise and sunset are known to be the most beautiful times, and there are descriptions of it as an open space with no separate admission fee. Winds are strong everywhere on Batan Island, so the grass on Vayang stays low and there are almost no trees. That opens up long views but also means there is no shade. Incidentally, the wind power plant in Batanes was reported to be on Mount Sumhao in Mahatao, not here, so if you go expecting a hill with windmills you may be disappointed.

This guide is for travelers staying in Basco who explore North Batan for half a day or a full day. Vayang is close to Basco Lighthouse, Valugan Boulder Beach and the Dipnaysuhuan Japanese Tunnel, so it is usually part of tricycle tours. It is grazing land for animals, so tell the road from private land and do not enter fenced areas. Rules for entering the ranch and operating hours are not in the sources, so check locally. The slope is gentle, but strong wind and mud after rain are dangerous, so watch the weather as you move. Besides Naidi Hills, Wikivoyage lists sights near Basco that you can walk to or reach on a short ride, including Radar Tukon about

away (a 360-degree view), a sunset trek toward Songsong and the hike up Mount Iraya. If you have time to spare at Vayang, you can add one of these. The hike to the summit of Mount Iraya is known to take about
3 hours
on foot.

blocks.title: Grass ridges running to the sea

children.text: The core of this place is the scene where gentle hills wind along and meet the sea. Climb to a high spot and try to capture the whole ridgeline and sea in one frame.
As the sun rises and sets the hills turn golden and the clouds redden. Travel guides give sunrise or sunset as the best time. Early in the morning there are few people.
Cows, goats and carabaos graze on the hills. One trip report describes the hills as a feeding and resting ground for the animals. Walk slowly and keep your distance so the animals are not startled.
It is a good place to spread a mat and have a snack or take a slow walk over the hills. There is almost no shade, so you need a hat and water, and you should take your trash with you.

Basco Lighthouse, the Dipnaysuhuan Japanese Tunnel and Valugan Boulder Beach are close, so you can visit them all in one go. It is fun to compare the view from the hills with the view from the top of the lighthouse.

blocks.title: Restaurant on the hill and a rest

children.text: One 2017 trip report says it had lunch at a restaurant on top of the Vayang hills. Operations and prices can change, so check in advance.
One guide says stargazing is also possible. But there are almost no lights and the wind is strong, so get to know the terrain during the day and plan safely.

items.title: Sunrise half-day route
items.subtitle: From Vayang to the lighthouse and the coast

children.text: Go from your Basco lodging to Vayang Rolling Hills by tricycle. Agree on a time with your driver the day before so you arrive before sunrise.
Climb the hills, wait for sunrise and photograph the ridgelines and sea. The dawn wind is cold, so bring a jacket.
Walk slowly across the hills, watching the grazing cows and goats from a distance.
Return to your lodging for breakfast and a rest.
Continue by tricycle to Basco Lighthouse and Valugan Boulder Beach.
Vayang to Basco Lighthouse is listed as about
2.7 km
, around
10 minutes
by tricycle.
Start a full-day tour with your tricycle driver from your lodging.
See the ridge views and animals at Vayang Rolling Hills.
Climb Basco Lighthouse and look out over all of Batan Island.
Return to town for lunch and a rest.
Visit Valugan Boulder Beach and the Dipnaysuhuan Japanese Tunnel, then return to Vayang around sunset.
For a full-day tour it is safer to change the order depending on weather and waves. If the wind is strong, see the hills before the coast.
Take a domestic flight from Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila to Basco Airport (BSO). Wikipedia says PAL Express operates the Manila route.
Small turboprop aircraft are used and flights are often cancelled in bad weather, so leave extra days in your schedule.
Round-trip fares vary greatly by season, and examples of about ₱10,000–20,000 have been reported.
There are reports that the pre-registration procedure for visiting Batanes has changed, so check provincial government announcements before you leave.
A guide says it takes about
10–15 minutes
by tricycle or van from central Basco or the airport. One 2026 travel guide said a whole-day tricycle rental around Basco is about
Some travelers rent a bicycle or motorbike and go on their own. Allow for the wind and slopes along the national road.
North Batan tricycle tours were listed in 2014–2018 trip reports at about
for two people. Prices may have risen, so agree on the price in advance.
It is also common to be introduced to a driver and guide through your lodging.

Wikivoyage describes the best time for Batanes as the dry season of roughly March–June, when winds and waves calm down. In this period there are fewer cancellations and the sky is clear, so the colors of the grassland and sea are vivid. Basco gets about 2,300 mm of rain a year, with August and September the wettest, and June–July are the hottest months.
After rain the hills can become muddy and the wind can grow very strong. In typhoon season it can be hard just to get around, so leave slack in your schedule.

Near Vayang Rolling Hills there are guesthouses and small hotels in Basco town. One travel guide lists lodgings such as Amboy Hometel, Dive Batanes Lodge and Marfel's Lodge as nearby. Wikivoyage advises that Basco is the only place on Batan with banks, so bring plenty of cash.

Meals are taken at restaurants and lodgings in Basco town. One 2017 trip report says it had lunch at about ₱375 per person at a restaurant on top of the Vayang hills. Food is expensive because many ingredients are imported, and coconut crab (about ₱800–2,000) is a dish that requires a permit, so eat it only at places that have one.
Going at sunrise or sunset gives the best scenery and fewer people. Agree on the time with your tricycle driver the day before.
There is almost no shade, so you need a hat, sunscreen and water. Winds are often strong, so use a hat with a strap.
Do not approach or feed the grazing animals. Do not enter fenced areas.
After rain the grass is slippery and muddy. Wear shoes with firm soles.
A tripod will shake in the wind, so set it low, and protect your lens from wind-blown dust.
Phone signal is weak, so save maps offline. Bring plenty of cash as well.
When you visit several places in a day, moving Vayang to early morning or around sunset gives better scenery.

In Basco town, agree with your tricycle driver on a time to be picked up. There is no good waiting place on the hills, and weak phone signal makes it hard to find each other. Leaving a whole-day rental with the same driver lets you spend time at your own pace enjoying the scenery.
Typhoons are frequent in Batanes and winds on the grassy hills are often strong, so postpone your visit in bad weather and leave slack days for small-plane cancellations.
The grazing land is where cows and goats live. Do not startle the animals or leave trash.
Do not enter places with fences or private-land signs. Check the rules for entering the ranch locally.
You can fall in strong wind and on slippery grass after rain. Children and elderly people should watch only from near the road.
It is dark and windy at night, so consult your lodging or a guide before any night activities such as stargazing.
There are reports that Batanes visitor rules, including pre-registration, are changing, so check official announcements before you leave.
